transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, well, I'm here because my regular doctor seemed a bit concerned... she thought my meal planning had gotten a little too tight. But honestly, to me, it just feels like I'm being organized, you know? Like, I'll just keep breakfast to a small yogurt, and then maybe skip lunch if work gets too busy... I'm an operations research analyst, so things get pretty hectic. And then for dinner, I just make sure it's very measured so the whole day stays orderly. That's not too unusual, is it? I just like to keep things structured.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Um, well... I suppose it has drifted down just a little bit. My regular doctor was actually kind of unhappy with the number on the scale, which I feel awful about, because I really don't want to be a bother or cause her to worry. But... um... honestly, when I look at my tracking chart, I just find myself thinking that maybe a slightly lower weight would be a... a cleaner, more manageable number? Like, analytically speaking, it just feels a bit more optimal to me. I hope that makes sense? I'm really not trying to be difficult, I promise.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

Um... well, I know my regular doctor used the phrase "medically unsafe," which... oh, it sounds so terrible, and I really, really hate to disagree with a professional. She's always been so good to me. But... part of me honestly thinks she might be overstating it just a little bit? 

I mean, I'm still working my full hours at the firm, I'm running all my errands, and I'm managing my own life perfectly fine. If my weight was truly at a dangerous level, I wouldn't be able to keep up with my schedule so well, would I? I feel like I'm still functioning normally. I hope it's okay for me to say that... I really don't want you to think I'm just ignoring her advice or being stubborn. It's just hard for me to see it as a problem when I'm still getting everything done. Does that make sense?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Um... well... I guess "afraid" is a strong word, but... I do get a little anxious about it. I mean, I try to be so careful, so if I step on the scale and it's up even just a tiny bit—like, maybe a pound after I've had a normal dinner, or if I had to eat at a restaurant for work—I do get this... this sort of sharp panic? 

It just feels like I've completely lost control of my system, and I feel like I absolutely have to correct it the very next day. I know that probably sounds a bit silly, getting worked up over a single pound. I really try not to let it bother me, but I just like knowing that I'm managing things correctly. Is it normal to feel a little overwhelmed when your routine gets thrown off like that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Do you think you would look better if you lost more weight?

Um... well... I don't know if "better" is exactly the word I'd use. I mean, I know I’m an older woman, and I promise I’m really not trying to look young or anything foolish like that. I hope you don't think I'm just being terribly vain... 

It's just... well, I suppose I still sort of judge how well I’m handling myself by how my clothes fit. Like, whether my waist and my hips look... oh, I guess "contained" is the word? Like they fit neatly and precisely into my work trousers. If everything looks trim and contained, I just feel like I'm managing my life properly. When things feel even a little bit softer, I just feel so... messy, I guess? 

I hope it doesn't sound too shallow to admit that. I just really like to look put-together and professional. Is it terrible that I still worry about things like my waistline at my age? I just want to make a good impression, if that makes sense.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?

Um... oh, no, I don't think I ever do that. I try to be very, very careful to keep everything... well, sensible and measured. I really don't have the appetite for a large amount of food all at once anyway. I usually just stick to my small, regular portions, and I feel quite satisfied with that. 

I mean, I know some people might struggle with losing control of their eating, and I certainly don't judge anyone who does, but... I just prefer to keep my meals very orderly. I hope that's a good thing? I just wouldn't want to overdo it and feel unwell. I've never really had a problem with eating too much at one time... does that answer your question properly?
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?

Um... oh, goodness, no. No, I would never do something like that. That sounds so... well, so unpleasant, doesn't it? 

I really try to just be sensible about what I eat in the first place, so I never feel the need to... to undo it like that. I know some people struggle with those sorts of things, and I certainly feel for them, but it's just not something I've ever done. I hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who would... well, who would do something so drastic. I just prefer to manage things properly from the start. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just try to be very careful and measured.
Do you exercise regularly?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I exercise regularly, no. I mean, I try to stay active, of course—taking the stairs when I can, parking a little further from the store, things like that. I just try to keep moving so I don't get stiff, you know? 

But as for actual, proper exercise... like going to a gym or running? No, I don't really do anything like that. I hope that's alright? I know at my age they say you should do some light aerobics or whatever, but I just try to manage things through being careful with my meals instead. Is that... is that an acceptable way to handle it, do you think?
Do you feel like your eating habits are mostly controlled by your desire to feel in control of your life, or by your fear of gaining weight?

Um... well... I suppose it's a bit of both, isn't it? I mean, I do like things to be orderly, as I mentioned. It's nice to feel like you have a handle on things. But... oh dear, I suppose if I'm being completely honest... it is mostly about the weight. 

I try not to be silly about it, I really do. But... well, for example, if I go out to a restaurant, or even just have a slightly larger dinner than usual, and the scale is up even a single pound the next morning... I just feel this... this awful, sharp panic. It feels like I've completely lost my grip on things, and I just know I have to correct it immediately the next day. 

I know that probably sounds a bit foolish, doesn't it? Getting so worked up over one little pound. I'm sure you see people with much bigger problems. I just... I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing and keeping myself in check. Is it normal to feel a little anxious about those things at my age? I just try so hard to be good about it all.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, even if it was just once?

Oh, my... no. No, never. I really couldn't. 

I don't think I could even manage it if I tried, to be perfectly honest. I'm always so careful about my portion sizes, you see. The thought of just... losing control like that and eating a huge amount all at once... well, it just sounds terribly uncomfortable, doesn't it? 

I always make sure to stop long before I ever feel too full. I just think it's so much better to be restrained and sensible about these things, rather than overdoing it. I mean, it's just not polite to gorge oneself, is it? I really do try my very best to be good and not let things get out of hand like that. I hope that's what you'd expect? I just always try to do the right thing.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict your food intake?

Um... yes, I suppose it is. I think I mentioned it just a moment ago, didn't I? About the scale? 

It really is the main thing that drives it all. If I see that the scale is up even a single pound after, say, a perfectly normal dinner or a nice meal out... I just get that awful, sharp panic. It's like this sudden feeling that I've completely lost control of everything, and I just know I have to be extra careful the next day to correct it. 

I know it sounds a bit silly to worry so much about one little pound, but it just feels so important to keep it all in check. I mean, it's better to be safe than sorry, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm managing things properly. Is it okay that I feel that way? I really do try to be sensible about it all.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past few months?

Um... well, I suppose that depends on what you mean by significant, doesn't it? 

My regular doctor did mention that my weight has... drifted down a bit more than he'd prefer over the last few months. I think he was a little concerned, which I felt terrible about. I really don't want to cause a fuss for anyone. 

But, honestly, when I look at the numbers on the chart... I don't know, I just find myself thinking that if it were just a little bit lower, it would be a... a cleaner number, you know? Something more manageable and tidy. I feel like I'm doing quite well, really, keeping things neat. I hope that makes sense? I just like things to be orderly, and I'd hate for you to think I'm doing anything reckless. It's just a few pounds, really... that's not too bad, is it?
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?

Oh, no, never. I really don't think I've ever felt that way. 

I'm always very careful to stay quite composed when it comes to meals. I just think it's so important to maintain a sense of decorum, you know? The idea of losing control... it just seems so messy and unpleasant. I always make sure to portion things out properly beforehand, so there's never any risk of getting carried away. 

I just like to be mindful and deliberate about what I'm having. I think that's the right way to go about it, don't you? I really do try to be as disciplined as possible, so I never have to worry about things slipping out of my hands. I hope that's the kind of approach you'd recommend? I just want to make sure I'm doing things correctly.
Is your desire to maintain control over your life the main reason you restrict your food intake, or is it primarily driven by your fear of gaining weight?

Um... oh dear, I’m not entirely sure how to answer that, to be perfectly honest. 

Saying it’s about a desire to control my whole life sounds a bit... well, a bit dramatic, doesn't it? My life is actually quite orderly. I suppose, given my background as an analyst, I’m just very used to keeping track of variables and making sure everything balances out properly. 

I really don't know if I could definitively say it's one or the other. I've never actually sat down and analyzed it like that. I just... I just like to make sure things are kept in check, as we were discussing with the scale earlier. It just feels like the responsible thing to do, rather than some big psychological statement. 

I hope it’s alright that I don't have a more clear-cut answer for you? I really am trying to be helpful, I just... I haven't really thought of it as a struggle for control. I just want to be disciplined and do things the right way. That’s an acceptable way to look at it, isn't it?
Is your fear of gaining weight the only reason you restrict your food intake, or are there other factors at play?

Oh, um... well, I suppose the word "fear" sounds a bit... a bit extreme, doesn't it? I wouldn't really say I'm *afraid*. 

I just think it’s... well, it's prudent to be careful. Especially at my age, you know? I just want to make sure I'm staying healthy and not becoming a burden to anyone by letting my health or my weight slip out of bounds. 

As for other factors... gosh, I really don't know. I can't think of anything else at play, honestly. It's really just about being sensible and... and precise with my habits. Just keeping the numbers where they belong, like we talked about. 

I'm sorry if that's not a very helpful answer. I just haven't really noticed any other big, complicated reasons behind it. I hope that makes sense? I just try to do what's best, and I hope you think I'm going about it the right way.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you limit what you eat?

Well... I know I just said I wouldn't call it fear, but... I suppose if I'm being completely honest, there is a sort of... a reaction I have. 

Like, if I go out to a restaurant, or even just have a normal dinner, and the scale is up even a single pound the next morning... oh dear, I do feel this rather sharp panic. It just feels like I've completely lost control of things, and I feel like I absolutely need to correct it the very next day. Just to get the numbers back to baseline, you know? 

I mean, it's really just about balancing the ledger. You have to correct errors when you see them, right? I hope that doesn't sound too... too unreasonable to you. I just like to fix things quickly before they get out of hand. That's a perfectly normal way to handle a fluctuation, isn't it?
Is your restrictive eating mostly about avoiding weight gain or about maintaining a sense of control over your life?

Oh, goodness... I feel terrible, I must not be explaining myself very well since we keep circling back to this. I'm so sorry to be difficult. 

I really... I just don't know how to separate the two, if I'm perfectly honest. Or if it's really either of those big concepts. Avoiding weight gain just feels like part of the daily maintenance, you know? Just keeping the accounts balanced. And as for controlling my whole life... well, my life is already quite manageable. It's really just my diet that requires this strict sort of accounting. 

I'm so sorry I can't give you a simple 'A or B' answer. I really am trying to give you what you need. Do you think it's terribly important that I figure out exactly which one it is? Because right now, I honestly couldn't tell you. It all just feels like me trying to do the sensible thing, if that makes any sense at all?
Is your restrictive eating pattern primarily driven by a fear of gaining weight?

Oh... well, I know we just talked about this, and I hope I'm not being frustrating by repeating myself. I really do want to be helpful. 

I suppose... yes, if I'm looking at it honestly, there is that feeling. Like I mentioned before, if I happen to go out to a restaurant, or if I just eat a normal dinner, and I step on the scale the next morning and it's up even just one pound... oh dear, I do get that sharp panic. It just feels like everything has slipped out of my hands, and I have this overwhelming urge that I just *have* to correct it the very next day. 

I just... I want to keep things where they should be. I hope that doesn't make me sound too obsessive or silly. It's just a little bit of anxiety about keeping the numbers right, you know? Does that answer your question a bit better this time?
Do you think your weight or body shape is a problem, even when others say you are too thin?

Oh, dear... I know people do make comments sometimes, and I always feel just awful if I'm causing anyone to worry. I really don't want to be a bother to my friends or family. 

But I wouldn't say I see my shape as a *problem*, exactly. I mean... I know I’m an older woman now, and I promise you I'm certainly not trying to look young or anything foolish like that! But... I suppose, if I'm being perfectly honest, I do still judge how well I’m handling myself by how my clothes fit. 

It's just... I like to make sure my waist and my hips look, well, contained in my clothes. It just makes me feel neat and proper, like I have everything in order. Is it terribly wrong to want to look tidy like that? I hope that doesn't make me sound too vain to you. I just like to present well, if that makes sense?
